paragraphs: (In the time of Shmuel’s father.) He is mentioned in Yevamot 115b, according to the Rosh’s reading, as having sent a bill of divorce to his wife; but Hyman says it is not known whether he was a Torah scholar.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson digital Yevamot 115b paragraph has אנא אנדרולינאי נהרדעא in the bill of divorce. David bar Nehilai is the name Hyman attributes to the Rosh’s reading. The digital paragraph does not establish that alternate reading’s printed form.

The saved Yevamot 115b paragraph mentions Shmuel’s father but names the sender Androlinai of Nehardea. Hyman’s David bar Nehilai is explicitly his report of the Rosh’s reading, not a replacement made in the digital Talmud.
